sections.html:
The Bitterroot Valley makes up Ravalli County, tucked into western Montana below Missoula County and against the Idaho line. Hamilton is its one city. Darby, Pinesdale and Stevensville are the towns, and Corvallis, Florence, Victor, Conner and Sula round out the map. Public land covers a big share, with parts of the Bitterroot and Lolo National Forests inside the line.

The valley keeps growing: 44,174 people in 2020, and an estimate of 48,582 for 2025. With 84.4 percent of residents in rural areas, plenty of sellers live well outside the towns, and for them the treasurer and the state revenue office matter more than any city hall. Owners occupy 76.5 percent of occupied homes, and 11.0 percent of the 21,062 housing units stand vacant.

No other Montana county currently carries a higher wildfire risk to structures than Ravalli, and over 7,000 homes and structures sit at risk in the greater Bitterroot Front project area. That Forest Service project runs along the mountain front above the main valley, from McClain Creek in the north to Trapper Creek in the south, and relies on thinning, harvest and prescribed burning to cut fuel. Pockets of dense trees killed by mountain pine beetle, Douglas-fir bark beetle and western spruce budworm make the picture worse.

Near the forest edge, buyers will bring up fire risk and insurance. A cash buyer who takes the house as is keeps that talk brief. Whatever route you choose, have your insurance paperwork and any brush clearing records on hand.

sections.h2: Treasurer or state: who handles what
sections.html:
Worth and class come from the state's Department of Revenue. Bills, payments and delinquencies belong to the Ravalli County Treasurer. Send valuation questions to the first and payment problems to the second.

Montana splits the bill into equal halves. The deadline for half one is 5 p.m. on November 30, and half two follows at 5 p.m. on May 31 of the next year. Paying everything in November is allowed.

Payment eventRule
First installment5 p.m., November 30
Second installment5 p.m., May 31
Penalty and interest2% penalty plus 5/6 of 1% interest per month (MCA 15-16-102)
Delinquent listPrinted each June, with notice that a tax lien is about to attach
Redemption window3 years after the lien attaches

Some 2026 due dates were moved, so check the date printed on your own bill with the Ravalli County Treasurer rather than assuming November 30.

Four slices of value apply to a primary residence or long-term rental in 2026, each with a different percentage:

  • Value through $378,000: 0.76%.
  • $378,001 through $756,000: 0.90%.
  • $756,001 through $1,511,999: 1.10%.
  • $1,512,000 or more: 1.90%.

Cabins and other second homes, short-term rentals and vacant residential lots all pay one flat 1.90%. On land, the rates are 2.05% for qualified agricultural land, 14.35% for non-qualified agricultural land and 0.37% for forest land, while a house and one-acre homesite on those parcels get the residential rate when lived in or rented long term. Qualifying means living there 7 or more months of 2026, or renting for 28 or more days at a time over at least 7 months.

Someone buying your house as a cabin will pay the flat rate, so your owner-occupied bill is not a safe preview of theirs.

Land adds a wrinkle. A listing with acreage should start with a look at how each parcel is classed, because agricultural, forest and residential land carry very different rates. A house and its one-acre homesite keep the residential rate only while someone lives there or rents it long term, which means the next owner's plans move the tax figure.

Your first move is a form: AB-26, sent to the Department of Revenue to ask for an informal review. You have 30 days counted from the date printed on the classification and appraisal notice. Values for the 2025 to 2026 cycle reflect January 1, 2024.

Skipping the informal step is allowed. Take the case to the county tax appeal board by filing with the county clerk and recorder, still inside that 30-day span. The county commissioners appoint this board, and it answers to no one at the Department of Revenue. Losing there leaves the Montana Tax Appeal Board and finally district court.

Do not stop paying during the dispute. Under 15-1-402, MCA, a protest counts only when it is in writing, filed with the county treasurer, and the disputed tax is paid by its due date. Miss either and a lowered value will not earn you a refund.

Good exhibits: your own value estimate for that date, a sale price within six months of it, a fee appraisal, comparable sales, or a builder's cost breakdown.

Start a folder with the latest tax bill, the classification and appraisal notice, any AB-26 or protest filings, and proof of homestead status, since buyers and the title company will want them. If the house is outside Hamilton or the small towns, which describes most of the valley, tell buyers early which taxing districts apply, since the county treasurer sends one bill and the state decides the class. Buyers who see a clean paper trail tend to move faster, and a cash buyer will usually close once the title work is clear.

sections.h2: If tax is owed when you sell
sections.html:
What you owe does not disappear when you sign a contract. Early in the August after an unpaid year, the debt becomes a lien, and nothing lifts it until every dollar of tax, interest, penalties and costs is paid. The county may keep it or sell it to an outside buyer, who receives an assignment certificate.

For three years after the lien attaches you keep title and can redeem by paying in full. Beyond that point, the holder can ask for a tax deed, and the property goes to public auction with opening bids at everything owed plus part of the appraised value.

A sale can still go through. At closing the title company pays the balance from your proceeds, and the deed is recorded with the county clerk and recorder alongside a Realty Transfer Certificate. Some owners can get help before it comes to that: the Property Tax Assistance Program for low-income Montanans, the Montana Disabled Veteran program and a land value assistance program for long-held family homes.

If you are behind, try this order: get the total from the treasurer, show the title company any lien notice that came in the mail, and request the payoff in writing before accepting an offer. Find out whether the lien was assigned to an investor, because that changes who receives the money.

faqs.q: When are Ravalli County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The statute says 5 p.m. on November 30 for the first half and 5 p.m. on May 31 for the second. A few counties shifted their 2026 first-half dates, so ask the Ravalli County Treasurer what your bill says.

faqs.q: Who sets the value of my Ravalli County home?
faqs.a: The state does, through the Department of Revenue. The treasurer takes the figure on your classification and appraisal notice and builds your bill from it.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days, counted from the date on your classification and appraisal notice. In that time file Form AB-26 with the Department of Revenue, or go straight to the county tax appeal board via the clerk and recorder.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay on time?
faqs.a: You owe a 2 percent penalty and 5/6 of 1 percent interest monthly. The debt becomes a lien, and once three years pass the lien holder can pursue a tax deed and a public auction.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Ravalli County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Since the lien stays with the property, it gets paid or settled at closing. A cash buyer can take the house as is, and the balance comes out of your proceeds.
